## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass over uploads on the Inputs and Context pages and fixed the
Inputs path end to end. A wrong-type, empty or over-10 MB file is now rejected
in the browser before it is read, with a plain-English reason and a fix. The
12-file cap holds across a multi-file drop, duplicate names are renamed instead
of overwriting each other, and a failed read says so. The server route applies
the same rules and returns honest status codes (400, 413, 404, 500) instead of
404 for everything. A headless WebKit audit at 375, 768 and 1280 px found one
real layout bug, a "Dismiss <file name>" button pushed off the left edge at 375
px, which is fixed. Context uploads (doc and skill) still have no limits. I
logged them as open items, because choosing a limit is a product decision.

## Work and rationale

The Inputs flow is `NewInputPanel.vue` → `ui.addInputScreenshots` →
`repo.uploadInputAttachment` → `POST /api/inputs/:id/attachments`. The client
had no checks. Drag-and-drop bypasses the picker's `accept` attribute, so a PDF
or a 300 MB file went straight to `FileReader` and then to the server. Task
screenshots already had a type and size rule (`SCREENSHOT_MIME`,
`MAX_SCREENSHOT_BYTES`), so inputs were the odd path out.

The client rules live in one pure module, `src/ui-app/src/lib/upload-guard.ts`,
which returns the sentence to show. A test asserts its size limit equals the
server constant, because drift would show a limit the server does not enforce.

The cap bug needed a design choice. The old code checked
`inputScreenshots.length` in the loop, but pushes happened inside
`FileReader.onload`, which runs later, so a 15-file drop queued all 15. Each
pick now reserves its slot synchronously and fills it on load. The write must
go through the reactive proxy from `inputScreenshots[length - 1]`. Writing to the
raw object updates the data but not the thumbnail. A failed read removes the
slot and adds a notice. Submit stays disabled while any slot is empty, so an
unread attachment cannot upload as empty bytes.

Notices go to `ui.inputUploadNotices` and render as a `role="alert"` block with
a Dismiss button. I chose this over a toast because the app has no toast for
form-level errors, and the notice stays visible while the person decides what to
do with the rejected file.

On the server I put the check in the route handler, not in
`saveInputAttachment`. The check needs constants from `server/attachments.ts`,
and `core` should not import from `server`. Validation runs before anything
reaches disk. The old 404-for-everything is why the UI could only ever show a
generic "not found" for an oversized file.

For Context I read `NewDocPanel` and `NewSkillPanel`. The doc upload
base64-encodes the whole file and the route takes it with no cap. The skill
upload reads the file as text with no type or size check. I did not invent
limits for either.

## Approaches tried

For the layout bug I first considered a max-width on the panel row. That would
hide the problem for short names and still clip long ones. The cause is that
`.btn-row` is a non-wrapping flex row aligned to the end, so a wide button
spills left, where the page cannot scroll. I kept the fix local to
`.ff-upload-followup .btn-row > *` and let the label wrap. A global `flex-wrap`
on `.btn-row` was broader than the bug, and other rows rely on the current
behaviour.

For the browser test I considered a real Vite dev server with a fake backend.
That needs a running server, which the acceptance criteria rule out. I followed
the stories QA pattern instead: mount the real components in jsdom against
seeded stores, serialize the markup, and inject it into headless WebKit with the
built global CSS.

I also considered moving the server check into `core/input.ts`. That would pull
`SCREENSHOT_MIME` into `core` or duplicate it, so I kept it in the route.

## Challenges and blockers

- **The first vitest run failed for the wrong reason.** Running `bunx vitest run`
  from the repo root gave a parse error on `.vue` files. The Vue plugin is in
  `src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`, so focused runs pass `--config` for that file.
- **The first browser run found a real bug.** The 375 px follow-up row put the
  Dismiss button at x = −121. I fixed the CSS and rebuilt with `bun run build:ui`,
  because the test reads the built stylesheet.
- **Size wording read badly.** A file one byte over the cap rendered as "10.0 MB …
  the limit is 10.0 MB". Sizes now round up to one decimal, and the limit shows as
  a whole number.
- **Not verified:** no live server, no real large file, and no device. The
  browser checks are headless only and use mocked responses.

## Key learnings

- The most useful finding was not visual. The server returned 404 for every
  upload failure, and the client never checked type or size. Checking the
  boundary you trust, here the route's status mapping, found more than looking at
  the rendered page.
- A counter checked before an async push is not a cap. Reserving the slot before
  the read is what makes the limit hold.
- Non-wrapping flex rows that align to the end are a common cause of off-screen
  controls at narrow widths. A long unbroken label is the worst case, so QA
  fixtures should include one.
- Context upload limits need a product decision before code. Filing that as a
  follow-up is cheaper than guessing a number and arguing about it in review.
